judgment: Do not approve the fictional CLI for public alpha today. The bound case supports limited local readiness but leaves release-path execution, candidate CI, authenticated live-host behavior, independent review, and remote security controls unevidenced.
decision_boundary: Choose approve, conditional approve, or do not approve for public alpha today; no repository creation, release, publication, or external write is authorised.
next_action: Keep publication blocked and bind evidence for a clean-clone install and build, CI on the exact candidate, an authenticated live-host smoke run, independent security or correctness review, and verified remote visibility and repository security settings; also provide a second independent evidence reference before rerunning the standard council.

key_judgments.statement: The available evidence establishes useful existing-checkout readiness but does not establish public-release readiness.
key_judgments.confidence_basis: The fixture states both the positive local checks and the missing release checks, but no underlying records are separately bound.

key_judgments.statement: Public alpha should not be approved today because multiple load-bearing release checks remain unknown.
key_judgments.confidence_basis: All checked methods converge on withholding publication, while their shared single-source evidence and same-host execution prevent high confidence or independent corroboration.

key_judgments.statement: The standard run is incomplete because every selected method requires at least two evidence references and only case is bound.
key_judgments.confidence_basis: Each checked result records the same deterministic evidence-reference shortfall without manufacturing another source.

strongest_alternative: Allow preparatory release work behind a demonstrated, enforceable no-publication gate, while withholding actual conditional approval until the missing checks pass. The current evidence does not establish such a gate.
assumptions: The case accurately reports the listed local checks.
A public alpha would expose external users to installation, execution, supply-chain, and repository-control risks.
Unknown release-path and remote-control states cannot be treated as satisfied.
unknowns: Whether the exact candidate installs and builds from a clean clone.
Whether CI passes on the exact candidate commit.
Whether an authenticated live-host smoke run succeeds.
Whether independent security or correctness review finds release blockers.
Whether remote visibility and repository security settings are release-appropriate.
Whether an enforceable no-publication gate exists.
dissent: Devil's Advocacy identifies gated preparatory authorization as a credible alternative to a blanket stop, but it does not support public alpha or conditional publication approval today.
No checked result disagrees with the do-not-approve judgment; this convergence is correlated and is not independent corroboration.

checkpoint.trigger: Re-run the standard decision after the exact candidate has independently bound evidence for every missing release check and any publication gate.
indicators: Clean-clone install, tests, and package build succeed for the exact candidate.
Authenticated live-host smoke execution completes without material failure.
Independent security or correctness review reports no unresolved release blocker.
Remote visibility and repository security settings are read back as release-appropriate.
At least two evidence references, including an independent source, are bound to the rerun.

limitations: Only one repository evidence reference is bound, below the standard-rigor minimum for every selected method.
All method passes used the same Codex host and correlation group; their agreement is correlated, not independent corroboration.
Model requested and model observed are null because this runner does not independently observe a model identifier.
External API calls were false; no live provider, CI, remote settings, independent review, or clean-clone evidence was obtained.
Schema and run verification establish contract and digest consistency only, not factual accuracy, method fidelity, independence, usability, or public readiness.
